title: Private deployments: VPC & On-Prem Reference, Day-2 Ops, Upgrades, and Customer Requirements
author: Ava Chen
body:
Purpose

This page consolidates our canonical guidance for Redwood Private deployments: VPC-hosted (customer-managed VPC + Redwood control plane), customer VPC peering/transit topologies, and fully on-prem / air-gapped packaging. It covers reference architectures, host and network requirements, Day-2 operations (scaling, backup, monitoring), and step-by-step upgrade and rollback procedures. Use this as the customer-facing technical reference and the operations runbook during onboarding and support.

Scope

- Audience: solutions engineers, customer SREs, platform engineers, and field engineering.
- Includes: network & firewall requirements, reference sizing, install and day-2 playbooks, upgrade/rollback, and a customer requirements checklist.
- Excludes: internal hosted API (see eng-platform docs) and model serving runtime internals (see eng-serving-runtime).

Owner & Contacts

- Document owner: eng-private-deployments team
- Primary contact: Ava Chen (Platform PM) - ava.chen@redwood.ai
- Escalation on-call: PrivateDeployments Pager (pagerduty) - contact via runbook page

Supported deployment modes

1. VPC-hosted Private (customer-managed VPC + Redwood control plane): recommended for most enterprise customers.
2. Private Dedicated (Redwood-managed HW in customer tenancy): for customers requiring reserved capacity with isolated tenancy.
3. On-prem / Air-gapped: full offline package for regulated environments.

Pre-deployment checklist (customer requirements)

Customers should confirm the following before scheduling an install window:

- Network and firewall rules (see table below)
- Admin IAM / RBAC user for installation and KMS access (if using CMK)
- DNS entries and TLS certificate (wildcard or SAN cert recommended)
- Persistent storage: NFS/EBS/LVM/CSI per reference architecture
- Time sync (NTP) and hostname convention
- Monitoring endpoint access (Prometheus, Grafana, Loki or vendor equivalent)
- Service account and API keys for cloud provider (if installing in cloud)
- Maintenance window for upgrades that require rolling restarts

Network & Firewall requirements

Table: required inbound/outbound access for typical VPC deployment (adjust per customer's network policy)

| Direction | Port(s) | Protocol | Purpose | Notes |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| Inbound (to control plane) | 443 | TCP | API (HTTPS) | Public endpoint if using Redwood-hosted control plane; otherwise ALB/NLB in front |
| Inbound (to nodes) | 22 | TCP | SSH (support only) | Often restricted to customer admin CIDRs |
| Outbound (from control plane) | 443, 80 | TCP | Container registry, KMS, telemetry | Allow required cloud endpoints or proxy |
| Internal (cluster network) | 2379 | TCP | etcd (if self-hosted DB) | Locked to management CIDRs |
| Internal | 10250, 30000-32767 | TCP | kubelet, node ports | Kubernetes default ports for health and services |
| Outbound | 9090, 3000 | TCP | Prometheus/Grafana push | For remote metrics and dashboards |

Recommended network topologies

- Small customers: single AZ with private subnets + managed NAT gateway; use private ALB and strict security groups.
- Enterprise customers: multi-AZ active/standby control plane with cross-AZ subnets and Transit Gateway for centralized connectivity.
- On-prem: colocate control plane and inference nodes on segmented VLANs, route to monitoring and backup networks.

Reference architectures (examples)

Note: sizes are prescriptive starting points. Final sizing must be validated during onboarding load test.

Small (pilot)
- Use-case: evaluation, low production traffic
- Control plane: 3x m5.large (or equivalent) VMs (2 CPU, 8GB)
- Inference pool: 1x GPU server (A10 or A100s-lite) or 2x T4s for light workloads
- Storage: 200GB per node

Medium (production)
- Use-case: steady-production, multi-tenant within single org
- Control plane: 3x m5.2xlarge (8 CPU, 32GB)
- Inference pool: 3x GPU servers (A10/A100-S or 4x T4s) behind a load balancer
- Storage: 1TB distributed, profile-based SSD for model cache

Large (high-throughput / low-latency)
- Use-case: high-throughput inference with strict latency SLOs
- Control plane: 5x c5.4xlarge or equivalent for orchestration and queuing
- Inference pool: 8+ GPU servers (A100 40/80GB or H100 where available)
- Network: 25G or 100G fabric and colocated model storage

On-prem packaging and installer options

Deliverables
- Airgap bundle: tarball containing container images (OCI tar), Helm charts, CRDs, and install scripts.
- Online installer: Helm chart + kustomize overlays with quickstart scripts.
- OVA/VM images (optional) for customers using vSphere.

Host requirements (on-prem)
- OS: RHEL 8.6+ or Ubuntu 22.04 LTS (kernel requirements noted in compatibility matrix)
- Docker/Containerd: containerd 1.6+ or Docker 20.10+ (as used by customer's k8s distribution)
- Kubernetes: v1.24 - v1.28 (consult supported matrix)
- Storage: 2 TB usable for model cache (NVMe recommended for large models)
- GPU drivers: NVIDIA driver 525+ and matching CUDA toolkit for accelerator fleet

Offline installation (high-level)

1) Customer provides offline registry access or local registry VM.
2) Copy airgap bundle to registry host and import images:

- Example commands (on registry host):
  tar xvf redwood-airgap-2026.tar.gz
  ctr -n k8s.io images import redwood-images.tar

3) Apply Helm chart with offline-values.yaml:
  helm install redwood ./charts/redwood -f values-offline.yaml --namespace redwood

4) Validate services: kubectl -n redwood get pods, kubectl logs for key components

Day-2 operations (runbooks)

Routine tasks
- Scaling inference pool: use the provided autoscaler or apply node group changes in cloud. Verify model cache warming and KV cache population after scale events.
- Backups: etcd (or DB) snapshots daily; model artifact snapshots weekly. Store backups in a hardened S3 or on-prem archive.
- Certificate rotation: replace TLS certs via Secrets rotation and perform rolling restarts.

Monitoring & alerting
- Required metrics: token throughput, request latency P50/P95/P99, model load times, GPU memory utilization, disk usage, pod restarts.
- Recommended alerts: request latency > 2x SLO for 5m, GPU OOM events, control plane pod crashloop > 3 restarts in 10m.

Incident playbook (short)
1. Triage: identify impacted services (API, model-serving, scheduler).
2. Mitigate: failover routing to alternate model variant or region; scale up worker pool.
3. Remediate: follow runbook for the failed component, collect logs, and open a postmortem.

Upgrade and rollback procedures

Principles
- Prefer rolling, non-disruptive upgrades.
- Always test in staging representative of customer topology.
- Maintain a tested rollback at every upgrade stage.

Pre-upgrade checklist
- Current snapshot of DB/etcd and application config exported and stored in safe location.
- Verify test suite and smoke checks pass in staging.
- Confirm maintenance window and customer acknowledgment.

Canary & rollout steps
1. Apply upgrade to control plane canary (single AZ node or 10% of control plane).
2. Monitor health checks and key SLO metrics for 15-30 minutes.
3. If green, roll upgrade across remaining control plane nodes with rolling restart.
4. Upgrade inference agents (GPU workers) in small batches, ensuring model availability and warmed caches.

Rollback steps (if issues detected)
1. Stop rollout and re-route traffic to pre-upgrade variant if available.
2. Re-deploy previous version using stored Helm chart and values file:
  helm upgrade --install redwood ./charts/redwood -f values-previous.yaml --namespace redwood
3. Restore DB snapshot if schema migrations were applied and are incompatible.
4. Verify system health and perform long-running request validations.

Common failure modes and mitigations
- Failed DB migration: restore snapshot and run migration in copy of staging cluster to debug.
- Model cache corruption: clear cache and trigger model re-pull; avoid deleting model storage unless instructed.
- GPU driver mismatch: keep driver/CUDA matrix in the install bundle and validate drivers before worker upgrade.

Customer requirements library (template)

Use the checklist below when qualifying new private deployment customers. Copy and share as part of the onboarding questionnaire.

1) Network & Security
- Do you allow outbound access to Redwood-managed registries or require an airgap bundle? (yes/no)
- CIDR blocks and admin CIDRs for SSH and support access
- TLS certificate authority and wildcard/SAN requirements
- KMS / CMK availability for envelope encryption (Y/N)

2) Compute & Storage
- Preferred GPU type and driver policies
- Minimum per-node disk and network bandwidth guarantees
- Preferred container runtime and k8s distribution/version

3) Observability & Backups
- Metrics ingest endpoint (Prometheus push/Pull) and retention policy
- Log forwarding (Loki/ELK/Splunk) and retention
- Backup storage location and retention (S3, on-prem archive)

4) Operations & SLAs
- Approved maintenance windows and blackout periods
- Contact lists for incident escalation and change approvals
- Required SLOs for latency and availability

Appendix A: Example smoke tests

- CLI: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://private-api.customer.corp/v1/health
- Model inference: POST /v1/generate with 1 short prompt; assert latency < P95 threshold and valid JSON response.

Appendix B: Useful commands

- Check pods: kubectl -n redwood get po -o wide
- Tail logs for controller: kubectl -n redwood logs deploy/redwood-controller -f
- Take etcd snapshot: ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl snapshot save snapshot.db --endpoints=<ENDPOINT> --cacert=<CA> --cert=<CERT> --key=<KEY>

Appendix C: Version compatibility matrix (summary)

- Redwood Platform 2026.1 - K8s 1.26+, containerd 1.6+, CUDA 11.8+, NVIDIA driver 525+
- Redwood Platform 2025.4 - K8s 1.24 - 1.25, containerd 1.4+, CUDA 11.4+, NVIDIA driver 470+
